t: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1631 as the tomb of Mumtaz Mahal, who died that year giving birth to their 14th child; in 1666 he was buried beside her.
The mausoleum was completed in 1648 and the whole complex is believed to have been finished in 1653, the work of more than 20,000 workers from Bukhara to southern India and Italy.
Its design draws on Timurid and Mughal tombs such as the Gur-e Amir and Humayun's Tomb, and its plan and garden are read as an image of paradise.
dyk: In 1942, and again during the India-Pakistan wars of 1965 and 1971, scaffolding was put up around the Taj Mahal to disguise it from bombers.
ev: Mumtaz Mahal dies in childbirth, and Shah Jahan commissions her tomb
Construction begins on land south of Agra obtained from Raja Jai Singh I
Shah Jahan holds the first ceremony at the mausoleum, on the 12th anniversary of her death
The mausoleum is completed; work on the rest of the complex continues for another five years
Shah Jahan, deposed by Aurangzeb in 1658, dies and is buried beside his wife
The restoration ordered by the viceroy Lord Curzon is completed
The Taj Mahal is designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
After directives of the Supreme Court of India, the Taj Trapezium Zone is set up to limit pollution

f.made: Commissioned by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan (r. 1628–1658); built by more than 20,000 workers and artisans under a board of architects led by Ustad Ahmad Lahori, the court architect, with the chief calligrapher Amanat Khan Shirazi
f.form: A mausoleum of brick and lime mortar faced with white Makrana marble inlaid with 28 kinds of stone, on a plinth 6 m high, with a dome 23 m high and four minarets over 40 m tall, in a 17-hectare complex with red sandstone buildings and a charbagh garden
f.where: On the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India; a Monument of National Importance administered by the Archaeological Survey of India
f.known: the tombs of Mumtaz Mahal and Shah Jahan; its white marble dome and four minarets; pietra dura inlay and Qur'anic calligraphy; the charbagh garden and reflecting pool; a symbol of love and of India; one of the New 7 Wonders of the World
